title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ignacio, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights Near Ignacio, CO | San Juan Basin
metaDescription: Own coalbed methane minerals near Ignacio in La Plata County? We price San Juan Basin interests off your actual production history.
heroLead: Ignacio sits in southern La Plata County within the Colorado portion of the San Juan Basin, one of the longest-producing coalbed methane fields in the country.
intro: Mineral ownership in this area varies: some interests belong to longtime ranching families, others connect to allotment-era land history specific to southwestern Colorado. Whatever the origin of your interest, our process starts the same way, confirming exactly what you own through La Plata County records before discussing value.

San Juan Basin wells produce differently than the horizontal shale wells owners hear about elsewhere in the state, with a slower buildup and a long, gradual decline that has kept many interests here paying steadily for two decades or more.

sections.heading: Understanding your specific ownership
paragraphs: Because ownership history in this part of the state can be more complex than a standard homestead-era severance, we take extra care confirming your exact interest and its origin through recorded La Plata County documents before pricing anything.

sections.heading: How Fruitland coal wells decline
paragraphs: Coalbed methane wells here typically produce water first, gas volumes build over months, and the eventual decline is gradual rather than steep. That long, gentle curve is why mature San Juan Basin interests often hold more value than owners initially expect.

sections.heading: Confirming current operator and unit status
paragraphs: San Juan Basin assets have changed hands between operators multiple times over the decades. We verify the current operator of record and confirm your division order matches actual current unit participation before finalizing an offer.

sections.heading: Confirming your interest is not encumbered
paragraphs: Before finalizing any offer, we confirm there are no outstanding liens, judgments, or competing claims recorded against your La Plata County mineral interest. This protects both sides and is a standard part of every transaction we close, not an extra step reserved for complicated cases.

faqs.question: Why does my well still produce after so many years?
faqs.answer: Fruitland coal wells in the San Juan Basin have historically long, gradual decline curves, so extended production runs are typical for this field.

faqs.question: My ownership history is complicated. Can you still help?
faqs.answer: Yes, we do the extra title research needed to confirm exactly what you own before making an offer.

faqs.question: Does a change in operator name over the years affect my ownership?
faqs.answer: No, it just reflects the basin's history of asset sales between companies. We confirm the current operator before pricing.

faqs.question: How do you make sure there are no other claims against my interest?
faqs.answer: We run a lien and title search through La Plata County records as a standard part of every transaction before closing.
